papers.title: $\delta$-derivations of simple finite-dimensional Jordan superalgebras
papers.abstract: We describe non-trivial $\delta$-derivations of semisimple finite-dimensional Jordan algebras over an algebraically closed field of characteristic not $2$, and of simple finite-dimensional Jordan superalgebras over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$. For these classes of algebras and superalgebras, non-zero non-trivial $\delta$-derivations are shown to be missing for $\delta\notin\{ 0,\frac12,1\}$, and we give a complete account of $\frac12$-derivations.

papers.title: Quotient rings and fields of integers from the metric geometry point of view
papers.abstract: The theory of Gromov-Hausdorff convergence is applied to sequences of quotient rings of integers, leading to the existence of limit rings as the Gromov-Hausdorff limits. It is also shown that such {\it limit rings} can be endowed with an order relation, although they are not ordered fields. When the construction restricts to quotients $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ with $p$ prime, the limits are fields. The relation of those limits with the field of the real numbers $\mathbb{R}$ is discussed, showing that the limit fields are dense in $\mathbb{R}$ but they cannot be identified with $\mathbb{R}$ or with the rational field $\mathbb{Q}$, at least when $\mathbb{R}$ and $\mathbb{Q}$ are endowed with the usual order relations and metric structures, neither they can be identified with the $p$-adic number system. It is also shown that the limit rings and fields have an ordinal larger than the reals and that they are endowed with an Archimedean absolute value function.

papers.title: Invariant factors from products of cyclotomic polynomials, with applications
papers.abstract: Let $f,g\in\mathbb{Z}[t]$ be products of cyclotomic polynomials such that either $g/\gcd(f,g)$ or $f/\gcd(f,g)$ (or both) is squarefree. We give explicit formulae for the invariant factors of $f(C_g)$, where $C_g$ is the companion matrix of $g$, expressing them in terms of the indices and multiplicities of the cyclotomic factors of $f$ and $g$. A more compact formula holds for the circulant case $g(t)=t^n-1$, assuming that every cyclotomic factor shared by $f$ and $g$ has multiplicity $1$ in $f$. We discuss applications to several topics, including abelianizations of cyclically presented groups, homology groups of cyclic branched covers of knots, adjacency matrices and shifted graph Laplacians, $K$-theory, and Smith forms of matrix powers. For example, for two families of hyperbolic knots we give the first integral homology in every covering degree; or, when $g$ is squarefree, we determine the least eventual period of the Smith forms of powers of $f(C_g)$.

papers.title: The zero divisor and augmentation conjectures for medial quandle rings
papers.abstract: For quandle rings, Bardakov--Passi--Singh and Elhamdadi--Nunez--Singh respectively formulated an analogue of Kaplansky's zero divisor conjecture and a weakened analogue of Kaplansky's idempotent conjecture involving the augmentation map. In this note, we verify these conjectures for medial quandles. The latter holds for a larger class of quandles; we characterize integral domains over which the statement holds for this class. We also characterize integral domains of characteristic 0 over which the statement holds for a given finite Alexander quandle.

papers.title: On the Fomin-Kirillov algebras
papers.abstract: The Fomin-Kirillov algebras $\mathcal{FK}_n$ are shown to be infinite-dimensional for $n\geq 6$. By computer calculations, we find an explicit nonzero primitive element of degree 14 in the identity component of $\mathcal{FK}_6$. For every $n\geq 6$, the existence of such an element implies that $\mathcal{FK}_n$ contains a polynomial subalgebra and is therefore infinite-dimensional, and that the canonical homomorphism from $\mathcal{FK}_n$ onto its associated Nichols algebra is not an isomorphism.

papers.title: Identities and isomorphisms of finite graded matrix algebras
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb{F}$ be a finite field and let $G$ be a group such that every finite subgroup of $G$ is cyclic. In this paper we classify the division gradings by cyclic groups on matrix algebras over $\mathbb{F}$. This yields the classification of the $G$-gradings on these algebras. Moreover if $G$ is abelian we prove that two matrix algebras over $\mathbb{F}$ with $G$-gradings satisfy the same graded identities if and only if they are isomorphic as graded algebras.

papers.title: Weak del Pezzo surfaces are characterized by the existence of $2$-tilting bundles
papers.abstract: For $d\geq1$, a tilting bundle on a regular proper $d$-dimensional variety over a field is called $d$-tilting if its endomorphism algebra has global dimension $d$, the smallest possible value. We prove that, over any field, the existence of a $d$-tilting bundle implies that the anticanonical bundle is semiample and big, and hence the variety is weak Fano. Moreover, the endomorphism algebra is $d$-representation tame. Conversely, every weak del Pezzo surface over an algebraically closed field of arbitrary characteristic admits a $2$-tilting bundle. Thus a smooth projective surface over such a field admits a $2$-tilting bundle if and only if it is a weak del Pezzo surface. This proves the variety case of Chan's conjecture, originally formulated in characteristic zero, and extends it to arbitrary characteristic. As an application, we construct a non-commutative crepant resolution (NCCR) of the anticanonical ring of any regular proper $d$-dimensional variety over any field admitting a $d$-tilting bundle. The NCCR is the endomorphism algebra of the pulled-back bundle on the total space of the canonical bundle. In particular, we obtain NCCRs of anticanonical cones over Du Val del Pezzo surfaces over algebraically closed fields of arbitrary characteristic. These NCCRs are the $3$-Calabi--Yau completions of the endomorphism algebras of $2$-tilting bundles on the minimal resolutions, extending the known construction for smooth del Pezzo surfaces to the Du Val case.

papers.title: Artin-Schelter Gorenstein property of Hopf Galois extensions
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the homological properties of the faithfully flat Hopf Galois extension $A \subseteq B$. It establishes that when $B$ is a noetherian affine PI algebra and $A$ is AS Gorenstein, $B$ inherits the AS Gorenstein property. Furthermore, we demonstrate that injective dimension serves as a monoidal invariant for AS Gorenstein Hopf algebras. Specifically, if two such Hopf algebras have equivalent monoidal categories of comodules, then their injective dimensions are equal.

papers.title: Orthogonal completion of algebraic systems
papers.abstract: The paper considers the generalization of the construction of orthogonal completion to all semiprime linear algebras (systems), its implementation in maximal systems of quotients similar to the symmetric Martindale ring of quotients for known examples of their description in terms of algebras of quotients of graded Lie algebras and technical results for applying the orthogonal completion method to them.

papers.title: Exact sequences of representation categories of weak Hopf algebras
papers.abstract: We study exact sequences of representation categories of weak Hopf algebras over an arbitrary field. Given a sequence $A\overset{k}{\to} B\overset{\pi}{\to} H$, where $A$ and $B$ are weak Hopf algebras and $H$ is a Hopf algebra, we develop verifiable algebraic conditions on $k$ and $\pi$ under which there is an exact sequence $\mathrm{Rep}(H)\to\mathrm{Rep}(B)\to\mathrm{Rep}(A)$ of tensor categories in the sense of Brugui\`eres and Natale (2011). Along the way, we develop a generalization of the restriction of scalars functor for maps $\pi:B\to H$ between associative algebras satisfying a weakened multiplicativity constraint depending on a relatively separable subalgebra $B_r\subseteq B$, as well as a theory of kernels and cokernels for weak Hopf algebras. We, in particular, find that the cokernel of a weak Hopf algebra homomorphism $k:A\to B$ always exists, is a Hopf algebra, and the cokernel map is surjective when $A$ is connected. We conclude by studying examples of such exact sequences built from groupoids, formal ribbon extensions of quasitriangular weak Hopf algebras, and cocycled crossed products of a Hopf algebra acting weakly on a weak Hopf algebra.

papers.title: Quasi-derivations of Block Lie algebras $\mathcal{B}(q)$
papers.abstract:
We compute quasi-derivations of Block Lie algebras $\mathcal{B}(q)$. In particular, we prove that $\mathcal{B}(q)$ has various nontrivial quasi-derivations, i.e., quasi-derivations different from derivations and $\delta$-derivations. As corollaries, we obtain a complete description of $\delta$-derivations, $\delta$-biderivations, and transposed $\delta$-Poisson structures on $\mathcal{B}(q)$ for $\delta
otin\{0;1\}$. In particular, for $\delta
otin\{0;1\}$, $\mathcal{B}(q)$ up to isomorphism admits only one nontrivial transposed $\delta$-Poisson structure if $q\in\mathbb Z$, and $\mathcal{B}(q)$ does not admit nontrivial transposed $\delta$-Poisson structures if $q
otin\mathbb Z$.
